title: Round 8 Post Qualifying Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome, everyone, to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following qualifying here at Monza. Joining us in P3 from DAMS Lucas Oil is Nicola Lacorte, in second place, from TRIDENT, is Matteo De Palo; and also from TRIDENT, capturing his third pole of the season, is Freddie Slater. Freddie, congratulations. You only had one lap to do it. How challenging was it?

Freddie Slater: Yes, definitely very challenging. Obviously, this morning we had, I think, around 30-degree track temperature, and this afternoon it was 55, so there was a big swing in track conditions and definitely a different balance. The team had to give us a car that could be in the window. At the end of the day, we had one lap to deliver, and we did the job and got nice track position as well. I'm very happy with the job we did, and I look forward to the weekend.

FIA Formula 3: Coming back to that track position, how did you and the team plan for it? It did look like the tow was pretty strong out there today.

Slater: Giacomo, the Team Manager, did a really good job, honestly. Hats off to him for what he did. He had all the situations covered. He kept me up to date with how much margin we had, whether we could do two push laps or one push lap, and the sequence. The run plan was changing every minute, every second. Hats off to the team for being calm under pressure and giving me the opportunity to go out there and do what I do. From then on, it was my job to put in a clean lap, in a good position with a good tow, and hopefully get pole at the end of the day.

FIA Formula 3: Were the tyres quite tricky out there today? Could you get more than one push lap out of them?

Slater: I think so, but we only did one, so we'll never know. We also only did one out-lap, which is not always normal. It was straight out into a first push, which is not easy for drivers, especially when you have a corner like Turn 1 as the first braking zone. It definitely wasn't easy for anyone, and it all came down to execution.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on the pole position. Matteo, coming to you, congratulations on P2. How does that feel?

Matteo De Palo: It feels good. It was a good lap. It was not an easy session for me either. We didn't have many laps, so only one counted, and it was the right one. Positioning was really tricky, but, as Freddie said, it was well managed for me as well. I think I was in the right place and then also put together a really good lap. We missed out on overall pole position by three hundredths, so there is everything to play for on Sunday. I'm happy with the work we did today.

FIA Formula 3: It's a front-row lockout for TRIDENT. What does that mean to you and the team?

De Palo: It's always good to start from the front row, especially here in Monza for me and the team, because there is an Italian connection for both of us. It's really nice. Especially for me, coming from some difficult rounds, it feels like redemption because I haven't been able to show many things lately due to circumstances outside my control. So, yes, it's definitely nice.

FIA Formula 3: It's your home race as well. What has the fan atmosphere been like?

De Palo: It's been crazy so far. Yesterday, we had a couple of fan zones, and it was really nice to have everyone here. There were also quite a lot of people at the track today watching us, so it was really good.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations.

De Palo: Thank you very much.

FIA Formula 3: Nicola, coming to you next, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your lap?

Nicola Lacorte: As Freddie said, we only had one push lap in the end, which was not ideal for the tyres or for what we had planned. Of course, you have to get the most out of it, and that's what the team and I did. I think pole was really difficult today, but we did what we could. My lap started well with a good tow. As you said, it was very powerful. Unfortunately, I finished without a tow because the car in front of me went off, so I was on my own for the rest of the lap. I'm really happy with the pace because it will also be important to have good pace without a tow tomorrow. I think we did a really good job, considering the season so far.

FIA Formula 3: Trying to strike the balance between having the right amount of downforce on the car and also having good straight-line speed, was it challenging to find that balance?

Lacorte: I think the best option is to have a tow, even though you know you're going to lose some downforce in fast corners like the Lesmos and Ascari. You just need to deal with it, get the most out of those fast corners, and take the advantage on the straights.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P3.

title: QUALIFYING: Impressive Slater takes pole with title rival Ugochukwu down the order in Monza
excerpt:
Freddie Slater took the Aramco Pole Position Award in phenomenal style in Monza, completing a 1:38.114 in Group B to beat TRIDENT teammate Matteo De Palo to the top prize.

De Palo set the pace in Group A with a 1:38.143, where Slater’s title rival Ugo Ugochukwu hit trouble and wound up in P10. The Italian will line up on the front row, while Nicola Lacorte will start in third after finishing second in Group B.

GROUP A

It was a slow start to the session but the drivers started to venture out with five minutes to go.

This gave most of them time for just one flying lap, with Hiyu Yamakoshi fastest on a 1:38.261. Taito Kato was just 0.014s behind but ahead of Fernando Barrichello in P3.

Critically, title contender Ugo Ugochukwu had a wide moment at Turn 1, and as a result ended up. Unfortunately for the Campos Racing driver he had no time to start another lap, having taken the chequered flag.

Matteo De Palo was one of the few who was able to get a second lap, and he went to P1 with a 1:38.143, beating Kanato Le to provisional pole by 0.020s.

Kato wound up third ahead of Yamakoshi and Barrichello, as Tuukka Taponen rounded out the top six.

With the final runs complete, Ugochukwu wound up in P10, leaving him with an uphill task for both races.

GROUP B

De Palo’s 1:38.143 was the time to beat, and just like the previous group, the drivers stayed in the pitlane until the final few minutes of the session.

They all had time for just one flying lap and it was Freddie Slater that shone the brightest with a 1:38.114, beating Nicola Lacorte by 0.236s.

Ernesto Rivera was third ahead of MP Motorsport duo Alessandro Giusti and Mattia Colnaghi as Pedro Clerot rounded out the top six.

Slater’s time was good enough to take pole position ahead of his TRIDENT teammate De Palo, with Lacorte set to start P3.

For Saturday’s Sprint Race, Taponen will start from reverse grid pole, with Clerot joining him on the front row.

That wraps up the Monza action for today, with the drivers set to return to the track tomorrow for the Sprint Race at 09:30 local time.

title: Ugo Ugochukwu handed grid penalty for both Monza races
excerpt:
Following the conclusion of Practice in Monza, Ugo Ugochukwu has been handed a grid penalty for causing a collision.

The Campos Racing driver was alleged to have caused a collision with Car 6 belonging to TRIDENT driver Matteo De Palo.

After the session, the Stewards heard from both drivers and team representatives and examined video evidence.

The Stewards determined that Car 2 had crowded Car 6 off the circuit and was therefore wholly at fault for the collision, breaching Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.

As a result, they applied a five-place grid penalty to the Campos driver. Ugochukwu will serve the penalty in both the Sprint and Feature Races this weekend in Monza.

title: ‘The car is quick’ says Giusti after ending Monza Free Practice on top
excerpt:
Alessandro Giusti reflected on a strong Free Practice session in Monza where he ended up with the fastest time

Alessandro Giusti was fastest in the Monza Free Practice and is hoping for more of the same in Qualifying. However, he does not believe pole position is vital to him having a good weekend in Italy.

The Frenchman’s 1:37.445 was the quickest time of the session, and impressively for MP Motorsport, he led a 1-2-3 for the team with Tuukka Taponen and Mattia Colnaghi in behind.

Speaking in the paddock afterwards, Giusti was impressed by their performance in what he felt was a largely clean session.

“It was good, it was decent,” said Giusti. “We executed well and we did a good lap. We had a good tow and the car is quick so just need the same for quali.

“Everyone wants a tow because in Monza it's nearly not possible to do a good lap without the tow, so everyone wants to have a clear tow and that's what I had.

“It was quite a clean FP but I think quali will be even more messy but I hope it will be safe for everyone and we can all have good laps.”

Giusti ended up with the fastest time in this morning's Monza Free Practice

Giusti set his time with the Soft tyres that they will be using in Qualifying after starting the session on their carry over Hards from the Madrid test.

The Williams Driver Academy member was happy to get a feel for the car on the softer compound going into the pole position shootout later today.

"I think there was quite a big gain on the softer tyre, it was really good,” Giusti continued. “I think the track was quick, and we were easily a second quicker than last year’s FP.

READ MORE

PRACTICE: Giusti leads strong MP Motorsport 1-2-3 at Monza opener

2026 Monza Qualifying Groups Drawn

“I think we will be a bit slower for quali because of the hot temperature, but anyway it doesn't change anything, it will be the same for everyone so we just need to do our job.”

Looking ahead to Qualifying, Giusti is set to run in Group B, and while he says he will be looking for a tow, he feels that getting in a clean lap is more important in the battle for top spot.

“Last year it was not that messy to be honest, everyone got a clean lap,” he said. “I think this year the goal is to have the same quali. It will be easier for everyone but I mean everyone wants a tow of like one or two seconds, something like this.

The French driver is hoping for a clean qualifying session this afternoon

“Around here you don't have so many corners, there is a lot of high speeds, so a good tow is needed, but if it's a mess it's better to do a lap as well.

“So if you had the choice of having a tow but doing no laps and having no tow but doing laps, it would be the second choice, so that's something we need to be good at and we need to look for in quali.”

READ MORE

PREVIEW: All to play for in Round 8 at Monza

‘Determined’ Badoer aiming to maximise performance at ‘special’ home race weekend in Monza

As for his goals in the afternoon session, Giusti acknowledges pole position would be nice, but that around Monza, it is not the be all and end all.

“To get pole would be nice but here it's not the fastest always with pole,” he concludes. “I feel like I just need to be in the good group for the race. Last year the winner never started on the front row, so I mean just start in a good position would be nice.

“I would be happy with a place in the top six but if it's pole for sure we'll take it, it's two points and to do pole in Monza, my origin being a bit Italian, it would be good to get it here, so I'll be happy.”

Next Up

title: PRACTICE: Giusti leads strong MP Motorsport 1-2-3 at Monza opener
excerpt:
Alessandro Giusti led the way for MP Motorsport at the Monza Free Practice, topping the timesheets with a 1:37.445

Tuukka Taponen set the early benchmark of a 1:40.020, with his MP teammate Giusti half a second behind in P2.

Noah Stromsted then reduced the gap to Taponen to 0.337s as PREMA Racing debutant Alex Powell went up to P3.

Hitech’s Jin Nakamura then took over at the top but was quickly demoted to P2 by Mattia Colnaghi, who completed a 1:39.467.

The times were starting to pour in quickly as Hiyu Yamakoshi went to within 0.064s off Colnaghi. However, on his next lap, Taponen regained top spot with a 1:39.150.

Title hopeful Ugo Ugochukwu then went quickest on a 1:38.883, putting him 0.108s clear of AIX Racing’s Yevan David.

But Taponen was once again showing his strong pace as he went back to P1, this time on a 1:38.444, as Taito Kato followed him across the line to go to second, albeit 0.405s behind.

The ART Grand Prix driver reduced the gap to 0.202s on his next lap, while his teammate Kanato Le jumped up to third.

Taponen improved to a 1:38.437 but his lead was reduced with Van Amersfoort Racing’s Yamakoshi just 0.088s behind in P2.

With just over 14 minutes to go in the session, the teams fitted the Soft tyre on their cars as they prepared for some qualifying simulation laps.

The drivers returned to the track with less than 10 minutes left of Practice, with Campos Racing’s Ernesto Rivera going quickest on a 1:37.901.

MP were showing great form as Giusti set the Formula 3 lap record around Monza with a 1:37.445 to lead teammate Taponen by 0.232s.

Colnaghi then made it a 1-2-3 for the Dutch team at the chequered flag, just as Ugochukwu and Matteo De Palo made contact down the main straight, leaving both cars by the side of the road with damage.

That brought an end to a strong session for MP with Giusti ahead of Taponen and Colnaghi. Gerrard Xie was fourth for DAMS Lucas Oil ahead of Rivera.

David was sixth ahead of Le and Stromsted, with Nicola Lacorte in ninth as VAR’s Bruno del Pino rounded out the top 10.

That wraps up the session with Group A set to hit the track for qualifying at 14:00 local time, before Group B get going at 14:20.

title: 2026 Monza Qualifying Groups Drawn
excerpt:
Following Thursday evening’s FIA Formula 3 drivers’ briefing in Monza, the Qualifying groups for Friday’s session have been decided.

It was confirmed that Group A will include all of the even-numbered cars, while Group B will feature those with odd numbers.

Group A is scheduled to take to the track first for the opening 10 minutes of running, which is set to get underway at 14:00 local time on Friday, with Group B set to follow at 14:20.

The grid will then be formed by an aggregated result as the driver with the quickest time takes Pole Position for the Feature Race. The fastest driver in the opposite group will join them on the front row in second.

Positions will then alternate between the two groups back and forth to fill out the remainder of the grid.

For Saturday’s Sprint Race, the sixth-fastest car in the second-fastest group will start the Sprint Race from reverse grid pole, while the driver in sixth from the pole-sitter’s group starting in second.

title: ‘Determined’ Badoer aiming to maximise performance at ‘special’ home race weekend in Monza
excerpt:
Brando Badoer believes making the right choices in Qualifying and the races are the keys to success around Monza – as the Italian previewed Round 8 and his home weekend.

The Rodin Motorsport driver has had a strong campaign up to this point and currently sits fifth in the Drivers’ Championship with 71 points.

Looking ahead to the Monza weekend, Badoer says he is feeling energised after a few weeks off for the summer break.

“I'm feeling good and determined as always,” said Badoer. “Obviously it's a special one being in Italy, but at the same time every race is important and we want to maximise every opportunity.

“It was definitely a good chance to recharge the batteries, I had some good fun with family and friends, trained hard and now we are ready to be back and ready to race. So I'm really happy to be in Monza and to be racing in Italy.”

Badoer is aiming to maximise performance in the car this weekend

So what are the keys to success around the Temple of Speed? Badoer says it all starts with qualifying and making sure he has a good grid position for both races.

“I think a lot of adaptability and strategy, especially for quali,” he explained. “A lot of importance always goes to quali and in this case it's a strategic one as you need a good tow for a good lap.

READ MORE

LN4 Fusion takes over AIX Racing and is set to join 2027 FIA Formula 3 grid

“So we will try to be smart and make the right choices to get a good lap and have a good starting position for both races.

“But it's important to be competitive. Qualifying in the top 12 is essential and it's better if it's in the top five for Grand Prix Sunday. Obviously, pole doesn't mean you're going to win the race.

Badoer is not too focused on the championship fight despite still being mathematically in contention

“It's a challenging track for racing, a lot of overtaking opportunities with three DRS zones in this year. It doesn't mean you're done if you don’t have an amazing quali, but we are looking forward to maximising every session. That's what we are going for.”

Badoer is still mathematically in with a chance of winning the Drivers’ title but concedes with Freddie Slater and Ugo Ugochukwu 50 points ahead of him, his focus is just on delivering the best results from now till the final whistle in Madrid.

“I'm aware I'm still mathematically on the championship fight,” said Badoer. “But it's not something I really think about because I'm aware it's a big gap to close from Freddie and Ugo.

“It's possible, but I'd rather focus race by race and see where we end up on Sunday in Madrid. That's going to be a different story. For now it's important to maximise the weekend and not think about the championship. It's more their problem.”

title: PREVIEW: All to play for in Round 8 at Monza
excerpt:
Monza plays host to the penultimate round of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 campaign and there’s always drama at the Temple of Speed.

The season's end is rapidly approaching, and Championship is far from decided with Freddie Slater leading Ugo Ugochukwu by eight points heading into this weekend.

Here’s all you need to know about what will be a pivotal weekend in the title fight.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Free Practice gets the weekend underway on Friday morning, with the green light scheduled for 08:35 local time.

Qualifying is split into two groups around Monza, with each group divided by car number and the running order for both groups determined via random draw ahead of Friday.

Group A will begin the grid-setting session at 14:00 local time with Group B following immediately after at 14:20.

Saturday is Sprint Race day and lights out is scheduled for 09:30 local time. Sunday’s Feature Race brings Round 8 to a close, with the race set to get going at 08:15 around Monza.

Pirelli will bring the red-marked Soft compound tyre for the race weekend.

STAT PACK

The FIA Formula 3 Monza Feature Race has never been won from pole position

Fourth position is the most successful grid position to have, with the last three winners starting from P4

Frederik Vesti’s 2020 Feature Race win is the furthest back the Monza Feature has been won from, with the Dane going from P9 to the top step

Ricardo Escotto is back for AIX Racing for the final two rounds while Alex Powell will see the season out with PREMA Racing

FROM THE GRID – Matteo De Palo, TRIDENT

“It’s a really fast track. It's my home race so it will be a special weekend for me and as usual, it will be a very exciting race.

“Turn 1 is probably the best place to overtake, you just have to send it on the brakes. Qualifying will be crucial. It’s a key point to have a really good tow in Qualifying to achieve a good lap.

“Monza is already special, but with it being my home race, it’s amazing to see and feel the Italian people in the stands, it’s a very nice feeling.”

TECHNICAL PREVIEW

Pierre-Alain Michot, FIA Formula 3 Technical Director

“Monza always presents a unique challenge for the teams and drivers, with the aero demand much less compared to circuits like the previous round in Budapest.

“Straight-line speed is key to being fast and therefore braking and fuel demands are high. The biggest stopping point will be into the chicane that opens the lap.

“We will very likely see a lot of drivers seek out a slipstream in Qualifying however, as we’ve seen in the past, pole position isn’t integral to a good weekend around this famous venue.”

PIRELLI PREVIEW

Monza hosts the penultimate round of this year’s Formula 3 championship. As was the case last year, the Soft compound has been selected for the Italian weekend, alongside a carry-over of the Hard compound from the tests conducted at the Madring circuit. Throughout the history of the series, races at Monza have consistently generated front-axle graining. Drivers will therefore need to manage degradation across both axles in order to maintain consistent performance through to the closing stages of the race. However, should track temperatures prove particularly high, as has been the case at previous rounds this season, the graining effect could be reduced.

title: LN4 Fusion takes over AIX Racing and is set to join 2027 FIA Formula 3 grid
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion will join the 2027 FIA Formula 3 grid. The new team is backed by 2025 Formula 1 World Champion Lando Norris. It has acquired selected assets from AIX Racing, including entry for the 2027 F3 season and has confirmed René Rosin will serve as Team Principal.

Speaking about the team’s formation and entry to FIA F3, Norris explained more about the project along with the LN4 Legacy Programme, a driver development project alongside the new outfit.

Co-Founder Norris said: “I’ve been really lucky to have some amazing people around me throughout my career, and I know that getting to Formula 1 takes so much more than just talent. You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time.

“That’s what these two projects are all about. LN4 Fusion is about building a race team that can compete with the best in junior motorsport, with great people and a great environment for drivers to develop. The LN4 Legacy Programme is about helping talented young drivers get opportunities they might not otherwise have.

“For me, they naturally fit together. I want to help create opportunities for the next generation, both on and off the track, and hopefully make a real difference to young drivers coming through the sport.”

FIA Formula 3 CEO Bruno Michel commented: “I’m very pleased to welcome LN4 Fusion to the FIA Formula 3 grid in 2027, after they have taken over AIX Racing entry. To have reigning Formula 1 World Champion Lando Norris involved in an F3 team is extremely positive. LN4 Fusion is going to be a serious project that will bring a lot of experience and expertise. I am certain that they will do a good job next season.

“I would like to thank everyone at AIX Racing for their hard work the past three seasons.”

Team Principal Rosin added: "Motorsport has always been my passion and my professional life. I am thrilled to have the opportunity to contribute my experience to an independent, vision-driven sporting programme with strong backing, a clear long-term vision and the resources required to build it properly. Having Lando on board adds a further dimension to this project. He has come through the junior single-seater ranks and understands its demands. His involvement will make a real difference to the team.

"We want to develop a pathway through junior single-seaters and create an environment in which drivers, engineers and sporting personnel can perform at the highest level. My role is to focus on racing: building and managing the sporting programme, creating the right technical environment and helping the team become competitive."

title: WHAT TO WATCH FOR: The key talking points heading into Monza
excerpt:
This weekend’s action will be the penultimate race weekend of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 campaign, and the Championship fight could hardly be closer.

Freddie Slater leads Ugo Ugochukwu by eight points going into Round 8, and the duo will be hoping for a big weekend to boost their hopes of glory.

Here are a few key items you’ll want to pay close attention to this weekend in Monza.

SPLIT QUALIFYING

This weekend will see Qualifying split into two groups in the same manner as Monte Carlo earlier this season.

Group A and Group B will be decided ahead of on-track running, with the drivers split into two groups of 15 cars based on odd and even numbers. The order in which the groups will run will be randomly drawn prior to Friday’s session.

With the layout of the Autodromo Nazionale Monza, drivers will still be eager to gain a slipstream to the car ahead in order to maximise their flying laps down the numerous straight-line sections of the famous venue.

With 15 cars on track at one time, you can still expect things to get busy with the fight for ideal track position, but is grid position as crucial as you might think?

WHY POLE ISN’T EVERYTHING

Slater and Ugochukwu could hardly be separated during Madring testing

Since the first FIA F3 race at Monza back in 2019, the driver to start from pole position has never converted their grid spot into Feature Race victory.

In fact, fourth place is the most successful grid position in terms of victories in the Feature event, with three different winners going from P4 to the top step of the podium.

2024 Champion Leonardo Fornaroli’s P2 finish at home in Monza in his title-clinching race is the best finish for a polesitter. Brad Benavides (P4, 2025) and Liam Lawson (P7, 2020) are the only other occasions in which the driver on pole has finished in the points at Monza in the Feature Race.

A front row start around Monza therefore isn’t a critical factor, and overtaking is very possible and we could see even more this year with a new addition to the circuit...

READ MORE

How to Watch Round 8 from Monza: TV, Session Times and More

NEW DRS ZONE

There will be a new DRS zone for drivers to contend with this weekend, with an additional zone added between Turns 10 and 11.

The run to the final corner and Parabolica will now be an area of the track drivers can use the Drag Reduction System and offers a great chance of overtaking into the final right-hand sweep.

Fornaroli proved that overtaking is possible into the final turn, ultimately winning his Championship crown with a final-lap overtake at the final corner of the season.

This change to the track offers drivers even more of an incentive to shape for a pass, and the prospect of wheel-to-wheel battles lasting even longer around Monza is a tantalising prospect.

Don’t forget, the next DRS zone down the main straight offers an immediate right of reply for drivers to attack into Turn 1.

Inthraphuvasak is the most recent winner of the Monza Feature Race

TITLE CONTENDERS

The title cannot be won this weekend with the Madring finale hosting two Feature Races, but Slater and Ugochukwu will both be looking to stamp their authority on the title fight going into that final round.

Monza has hosted plenty of F3 title-deciding drama in the past. Victor Martins won the 2022 title in the pit lane after a thrilling race on a weekend that had seven different drivers vying for the crown entering the round.

The aforementioned final-lap pass by Fornaroli capped off an incredible 2024 campaign, but this season the Italian venue will not see an F3 Champion crowned.

With that said, both Campos and TRIDENT have enjoyed victories around Monza. Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak won for the Spanish outfit last year, while Sami Meguetounif secured 2024 honours for TRIDENT on home soil.

Slater is riding a wave of momentum having overturned the points deficit back in Budapest to lead the Standings, but Ugochukwu struck back in Madring testing, winding up fastest of all across the two-day event ahead of Slater, both topping two sessions apiece.

Monza won’t be the scene of a coronation for either driver, but both will have it in the back of their mind a big result here could set the tone going into the decider in Madrid.

title: FIRST IMPRESSIONS: What the drivers thought of the Madring
excerpt:
With two days of testing in the books, many miles and plenty of data accumulated, we asked the drivers what they thought of the brand-new Madring circuit ahead of its full debut next month.

Overall, it looks to be one of the biggest tests on the racing calendar, blending high-speed demand for full commitment with a need for absolute precision and a bit of bravery too.

Here is what the F3 drivers thought after two days of on-track running.

Freddie Slater – TRIDENT

“Honestly, what an incredible track. It's probably my favourite on the calendar. It's old school, it's got character, it's a really enjoyable track to drive, lots of little bumps you have to get right, very committed in high-speed corners, and one of the most enjoyable of the season. So I'm really enjoying it.”

Mattia Colnaghi – MP Motorsport

“Quite an interesting track, a bit of a street circuit, it can be compared to Melbourne but overall it's quite interesting and there something different in each of the sectors. I think it's going to be an interesting weekend.”

Pedro Clerot – Rodin Motorsport

“Fun track to drive, but very tricky. At the moment it’s still very low grip, but I'm having fun so far. Just getting to know the walls a little bit better, getting to the limit a bit more, but overall, quite fun.”

Ugo Ugochukwu – Campos Racing

“It’s an unbelievable circuit to be honest. We just finished Day 2 morning which was focused on all the qualifying runs and it's a very nice feeling when you get it right and the lap hooked up. I'm definitely going to enjoy it, and I'm sure it's going to be a great weekend.”

Tuukka Taponen – MP Motorsport

“It’s super difficult, also quite physical. On the long runs, it’s not easy. I’d say it’s one of the most difficult tracks I’ve ever driven, but still quite fun and flowing when you get into a rhythm.”

Kanato Le – ART Grand Prix

“I think it's quite a cool track, super close to the walls, and you have to be quite on the edge, but it's really fun to drive, and I think the race weekend it will be pretty close.”

READ MORE

Ugochukwu optimistic heading into title-deciding races after topping Madrid test

Slater thriving around ‘old-school’ Madring track after topping Day 1 of testing

Ugo Ugochukwu finishes Madring test fastest for Campos Racing

Ernesto Rivera – Campos Racing

“It's very tricky. I mean, it's very close to the walls, especially on the exits. La Monumental is super fun as well, you can feel the compression through the corner.”

Hiyu Yamakoshi – Van Amersfoort Racing

“It's quite similar to Macau, but this track is more tricky. I think it's really difficult to put everything together, but as always, the most important thing will be qualifying and keeping it clean.”

Alessandro Giusti – MP Motorsport

“It's been good, it's fun. It's a track that no one knows, so it's quite good to get up to speed, and there are a lot of different lines, different ways to arrive into the corners, so it's really cool.”

title: Ugochukwu optimistic heading into title-deciding races after topping Madrid test
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu ended Madrid testing fastest overall and has high hopes for the season-deciding rounds to come

Ugo Ugochukwu left the Madring with an unofficial FIA Formula 3 lap record, finishing the two-day event with the fastest time overall: 1:49.034.

The Campos Racing driver was quickest in both morning sessions in Madrid and was very pleased with the work he and the team carried out across the event.

It could prove crucial, with the finale taking place at the brand-new Spanish venue, with an extra Feature Race included.

Speaking in the paddock after getting out of the car on Day 2, Ugochukwu says that the team were able to be on the pace right away.

“It's definitely been a good test,” he said. “It's good to get back into the car after a little time away over the summer break and immediately I felt quite at one with the track.

“It's a very challenging circuit. We've had multiple red flags, so it'll definitely be a factor when we come here for the race weekend.

“But I definitely feeling good around here which is a positive note and hopefully we can bring this good pace into the race weekend for the last rounds.”

Ugochukwu set the fastest time of the Madrid test on the second morning of running

The new circuit caught several drivers out but with the fast speeds and tricky layout, the drivers were enthusiastic about the challenge posed by the Madring.

Ugochukwu echoed that and said that it was an exciting venue to drive, especially over a flying lap. He added that he was able to build into his fastest effort over the course of the test and get closer to the absolute limit.

“There's definitely not a lot of room. I think as we put more new tyres on the car we kind of pushed more and more and I think every lap was closer and closer to the wall. I felt that lap was nicely on the limit which is what you need around this place.

TESTING IN MADRID

Ugo Ugochukwu finishes Madring test fastest for Campos Racing

Slater thriving around ‘old-school’ Madring track after topping Day 1 of testing

Freddie Slater ends Day 1 fastest in Madrid for TRIDENT

“You're right on the limit, but without going over, which isn't easy. I’ll be trying to replicate that in quali on the race weekend.

"As with every street circuit there's no room for mistakes but around here there's definitely some corners which are very high speed and a bit blind, and so it's not so easy.

“Monaco is a different type of street track and challenge, while here there's more high-speed bits which can be a deciding factor when it comes to the race weekend.”

The American is confident that Campos learned what they needed to during the two-day event

With an eight point deficit to make up in the final two rounds, Ugochukwu will be hoping to have already overhauled title rival Freddie Slater by the time F3 returns to Madrid for the season finale.

It made the two days of testing all the more important, with the pair very closely matched across the season. In fact, they shared two sessions apiece at the top of the times from the four in total.

The Campos driver topped both mornings while in the afternoon it was Slater in P1 on both days. It sets up an incredible final few races, with Ugochukwu certain the team will have a strong platform for the last race of the season following their extensive work across the test.

“I think, we learned the little bits that we needed to. It was good to experience the real track because before we only had the sim to go off.

“We get a rough idea of how it's going to be but actually driving here I think the team can really see how everything correlates - how the tyres react around here, when it's best to do your quick lap - all the stuff we need to maximise in the final round.”

title: Ugo Ugochukwu finishes Madring test fastest for Campos Racing
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu finished the Madring test with the quickest time of all, setting a 1:49.034 to lead the field on the second and final day of in-season testing.

The Campos Racing driver topped the times by two-tenths of a second in the morning segment, while in the afternoon, Championship rival and current points leader Freddie Slater was quickest for TRIDENT.

MORNING

The session began with everyone eager to get some qualifying running under their belts but an early Red Flag was thrown after a spin for Fernando Barrichello at Turn 8. The AIX Racing driver recovered to the pit lane without damage and the session quickly resumed.

Campos teammates Théophile Nael and Ernesto Rivera then took turns at the top of the timing screens, the latter setting the fastest time of the test up to that point with a 1:50.108.

Taito Kato beat that effort before the opening hour was complete, logging a 1:49.673, which was then shaded by Yevan David for AIX with a 1:49.561 before the second Red Flag of the day was shown, with the Sri Lankan driver stopped on track, though he was able to recover to the pit lane.

The action resumed but was then stopped just as quickly after Woohyun Shin found the barriers at Turn 5 in the Hitech.

After his car was recovered, the morning session resumed with just over an hour to go and the improvements began to flow.

Ugochukwu laid down the quickest time of the test with 45 minutes to go, 1:49.034 putting him half a second clear of the pack.

Further improvements from several drivers followed before a Red Flag with just over 20 minutes to go, this time after Hiyu Yamakoshi found the barriers at Turn 11 having just gone second quickest to the Campos.

There was one final green flag stint, but nobody could better Ugochukwu’s effort. Yamakoshi followed in second ahead of Enzo Deligny for Van Amersfoort Racing, with Rivera and MP Motorsport’s Tuukka Taponen completing the top five.

AFTERNOON

Ugochukwu headed back out with several others in the early minutes of the afternoon and the American set a 1:49.790 to lead the pack. But a Red Flag then arrived as Fionn McLaughlin found the barriers at Turn 14 in the Hitech.

He was OK and his car was cleared, and the session resumed with two and a half hours to go.

Race runs were the focus in comparison to the morning session, and while there were several personal bests, there was no real movement at the top of the times as mileage was accumulated.

The Red Flag came with an hour gone, as TRIDENT's Matteo De Palo stopped on track. His car was quickly recovered, and the session resumed with an hour and 45 minutes of the test remaining.

But another quickfire Red Flag arrived as Mattia Colnaghi lost his front wing at Turn 7. All cars returned to the pit lane and action resumed, though another Red Flag arrived once again shortly afterwards.

A spin for Nicola Lacorte at Turn 14 and slight contact with the barriers brought a stoppage to the session, but the DAMS Lucas Oil driver was able to recover to the pit lane.

Running got back underway and as the clock ticked into the final 45 minutes there was movement at the top. Slater displaced title rival Ugochukwu at the top of the timing pages with a 1:49.685, just before another Red Flag was waved.

This time it was Kanato Le of ART Grand Prix who caused the stoppage at Turn 7 after contact with the barriers.

The session resumed with 25 minutes to go but there was one final Red Flag as Fernando Barrichello found the barriers at Turn 3. He was OK but the session was not resumed, leaving Slater fastest in the afternoon from Ugochukwu and Nael.

David was fourth for AIX ahead of Rivera, who ensured all three Campos’ were inside the top five. Pedro Clerot was sixth for Rodin Motorsport ahead of Deligny, Brando Badoer, Noah Stromsted and De Palo of TRIDENT, who completed the top 10.

FIA Formula 3 returns to racing action at Monza on September 4-6 for the penultimate round of the 2026 campaign.

title: Slater thriving around ‘old-school’ Madring track after topping Day 1 of testing
excerpt:
Freddie Slater was very pleased with his and TRIDENT's efforts on Day 1 of Madrid in-season testing

Freddie Slater was the one to beat on the opening day of in-season testing around the new Madring circuit. The TRIDENT driver set a 1:50.343 in the afternoon running to finish the day quickest of all.

The Audi Development Driver was very happy with his and the team’s efforts on a tricky opening day and says that he ranks the track amongst his favourites following a first taste of on-track action.

“I think it was a really positive day,” he summarised back in the paddock. “I think this track is incredible to drive, it's a bit old-school, got some interesting corners and it's got a lot of character to it. It's probably one of the most enjoyable on a push lap on the calendar.

“I'm just enjoying it. I'm having fun. Today has been a really positive day. I'm just learning about the track and trying to adapt my driving style to it and also adapt the car a bit to it.

“It's been a good learning day for the team, especially, which is very important, obviously, with a completely new track and no previous data to rely on. It's been a solid day so far.”

Drivers and teams turned up in Madrid with only simulator data to go off, having had no prior data around the circuit to utilise.

Slater was fast all day in Madrid and was very happy with the work he and the team carried out on Day 1

It made track time and run planning very important, something that Slater says he was able to achieve with TRIDENT across the day.

Speaking about how things unfolded from the cockpit, the British driver says it was about finding a rhythm around what is a high-speed street circuit.

"I've actually had a couple of experiences around street tracks, obviously, Macau, Monaco this year, and it's about going out, being on the limit, but not being too over the limit that you end up risking crashing.

READ MORE

Freddie Slater ends Day 1 fastest in Madrid for TRIDENT

AS IT HAPPENED: Follow all the action from the in-season test at the Madring

“I think that was very important this morning to build up to it, to get multiple laps under the belt so you actually could work out what was going on. I think it's been a positive way of building up to it. I look forward to tomorrow.

“But I love the whole thing. I think it's incredible. I think it's one of the best tracks I’ve driven. Like all the best tracks, like your Macau's, your Monaco's, the tracks that have got character, and I think that's what's the most special thing that they've done here. I can't name a favourite part, but I do like the Turn 5 and 6 chicane.”

The Audi Development Driver hopes to be on the attack once again on the final day as times should improve

Tomorrow’s running will be the final bit of preparation teams and drivers will get ahead of the penultimate round in Monza before returning to Madrid for the season finale in September.

Slater is hoping to replicate his opening day form but expects everyone to take a step forward, with unused tyres to play with on Tuesday.

“I think tomorrow you'll see probably a little bit more new tyres put on a lot sooner. I think probably two or three runs in a row maybe in the morning, which we normally see on the second day in the morning of these tests.

“I think the pace has been really strong today, especially considering what tyres we're on and compared to other people. So, a really, really positive day, honestly, as I look back on it.

“It’s a nice way to begin this final stint of the season. I think tomorrow is going to be lots of qualifying simulations, but also trying to get some race runs in, as today we had quite a few red flags that didn't help in that sense.”
